open_points.subject: document authority
open_points.text: “not accepted by the owner as a whole” while only “R0-06 to R0-14 are the owner's decisions”
open_points.question: Are R0-01 through R0-05 and the surrounding product boundary binding inputs for later states, or are they still awaiting an owner decision?
options: Treat only R0-06 through R0-14 as accepted
Treat the complete document as accepted
Stop until the owner accepts or revises the remaining text
open_points.default_guess: Treat R0-06 through R0-14 as binding and carry R0-01 through R0-05 as unresolved.

open_points.subject: project ownership of customer
open_points.text: “which customer it belongs to” and “missing name or address refused”
open_points.question: Must every project have a customer_ref at creation, or may a project exist without a customer?
options: Require an existing customer_ref
Allow customer_ref to be absent
Allow a free-form customer value
open_points.default_guess: Require an existing customer_ref.

open_points.subject: project and room writers
open_points.text: “staff, consumer service” versus “Cabinet Kernel and the operator also create projects and rooms”
open_points.question: Which named services may create projects and rooms: every consumer service, only Cabinet Kernel, or a configured subset?
options: Every service with a service token
Only Cabinet Kernel plus staff
A configured per-action set of services
open_points.default_guess: Allow Cabinet Kernel and staff only.

open_points.subject: service-token authorization
open_points.text: “a service that writes holds a service token”
open_points.question: Does possession of any service token authorize every non-artifact write, or does each token carry specific allowed actions?
options: Any service token may perform any service write
Tokens have per-action permissions
Only explicitly named services may write
open_points.default_guess: Use per-action permissions tied to the named service.

open_points.subject: Factory access to customer phone
open_points.text: “The Factory's WhatsApp link reads the phone from here” versus “Personal data ... readable by staff only”
open_points.question: What actor is the Factory, and under whose staff authority may it read the customer's phone?
options: Factory is a staff-authenticated client
Factory is a service allowed to read contact data
Factory receives the phone from staff outside Registry
open_points.default_guess: Treat Factory as a staff-authenticated client.

open_points.subject: planner producer
open_points.text: “planners by name only”
open_points.question: Is there a planner service that may authenticate and publish, or is planner merely a reserved owner-service name with no current caller?
options: A real planner service with a service token
A reserved owner-service identity only
Remove planners from the current producer set
open_points.default_guess: Treat planner as a reserved owner-service identity only.

open_points.subject: browser origin
open_points.text: “CORS admits exactly that origin”
open_points.question: What exact origin is admitted, and where is that value declared?
options: A required configured origin
A fixed origin named by the specification
The API's own origin only
open_points.default_guess: Require one configured frontend origin.

open_points.subject: open-read callers
open_points.text: “Reading projects, rooms, artifacts, validate and context needs no credential” versus action actors restricted to “staff, consumer service” or “consumer service”
open_points.question: May every caller on the allowed network invoke room, artifact, validate, context and latest-artifact reads, or are those actions restricted to the actors named in the table?
options: Any network caller may invoke them
Only the table's named actors may invoke them
Some routes are public and others actor-restricted
open_points.default_guess: Allow any caller on the loopback or private-network surface.

open_points.subject: create-project input
open_points.text: “the project with its identity — supplied by the caller or minted”
open_points.question: What complete input constitutes a project creation request, including the forms of name, address, customer_ref and optional project_id?
options: Structured name, address and required customer_ref plus optional project_id
Name and address plus optional customer_ref and project_id
An opaque project document
open_points.default_guess: Use name, structured address, required existing customer_ref and optional project_id.

open_points.subject: create replay equality
open_points.text: “an equal replay returns the existing project, a different one with the same id is refused”
open_points.question: Which fields participate in equality, and are normalization, server-generated fields, later corrections and customer erasure ignored?
options: Compare normalized creation inputs only
Compare the complete current project representation
Compare byte-for-byte request bodies
open_points.default_guess: Compare normalized creation inputs excluding server-generated fields.

open_points.subject: create replay after archival
open_points.text: “output ... status active”; “an equal replay returns the existing project”; “Archive is final”
open_points.question: What happens when create is replayed with the id and original content of an archived project?
options: Return the existing archived project
Refuse because the id belongs to an archived project
Return it as active, effectively restoring it
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing archived project without changing it.

open_points.subject: project card
open_points.text: “the project card ... with its rooms”
open_points.question: Which exact fields appear in a project card, and does its customer value contain only customer_ref and erasure state or any protected contact data?
options: Project fields plus customer_ref only
Project fields plus an embedded redacted customer summary
Project fields plus full customer data for authenticated staff
open_points.default_guess: Return project fields and customer_ref only, never contact data.

open_points.subject: project-list contract
open_points.text: “archived only when asked, in a declared order (L10), as one answer object”
open_points.question: What requests inclusion of archived projects, what is the named items field, and what exact ordering and tie-breaker apply?
options: Boolean include_archived, field projects, creation order plus id tie-breaker
Status filter, field items, name order plus id tie-breaker
Separate active and archived lists
open_points.default_guess: Use include_archived, a projects field, and creation time then project_id.

open_points.subject: project correction
open_points.text: “the project with the new name, address or customer”
open_points.question: Is correction a partial patch or full replacement, may values be cleared, and must a new customer_ref identify a non-erased Customer?
options: Partial patch with non-null values and a live customer_ref
Full replacement of all mutable fields
Partial patch allowing a missing or erased customer
open_points.default_guess: Use a partial patch; reject empty required values and unknown or erased customer_ref values.

open_points.subject: validate response
open_points.text: “exists, active, and why not (not_found, archived)” and “keeps both answers field for field”
open_points.question: What are the exact response field names, types and combinations for active, archived and unknown project ids?
options: Define the complete schema in this text
Import an explicitly reproduced legacy schema
Leave field selection to the next state
open_points.default_guess: Define booleans exists and active plus a nullable reason enum.

open_points.subject: context response
open_points.text: “id, display name, status, address, customer, created and updated times” and “keeps both answers field for field”
open_points.question: What are the exact field names and value shapes, especially address, customer and timestamps, and does customer mean customer_ref rather than protected contact data?
options: Define the complete schema with customer_ref only
Embed a redacted customer object
Return full customer contact data to authenticated callers
open_points.default_guess: Define an explicit schema using customer_ref only and ISO-8601 timestamps.

open_points.subject: customer creation
open_points.text: “the Customer with its identity (customer_ref) and contact data”
open_points.question: Who allocates customer_ref, which contact fields are required or nullable, and what happens on a duplicate reference or repeated request?
options: Server-minted customer_ref with name required and other fields optional
Caller-supplied customer_ref with idempotent replay
Either caller-supplied or server-minted, like project_id
open_points.default_guess: Mint customer_ref on the server, require name, and allow phone, e-mail and language to be absent.

open_points.subject: customer correction
open_points.text: “the Customer with the new contact data”
open_points.question: Is correction partial or complete, which fields may be cleared, and what validation applies to name, phone, e-mail and language?
options: Partial patch with explicit nulls for optional fields
Complete replacement of contact data
Only non-empty values may be changed
open_points.default_guess: Use a partial patch, keep name required and allow optional fields to be cleared explicitly.

open_points.subject: erased-customer representation
open_points.text: “answers that it was erased” and “erased ones only as erased”
open_points.question: What exact fields and marker represent an erased customer in read and list responses?
options: customer_ref plus erased true
customer_ref plus a status enum
A distinct erased-customer response type
open_points.default_guess: Return customer_ref and an erased boolean only.

open_points.subject: room model
open_points.text: “the room in the project”
open_points.question: What facts identify and describe a room, who allocates room_id, which inputs are required, and how are duplicate room creations handled?
options: Server-minted room_id and required display name
Caller-supplied room_id and required display name
Opaque room value supplied by the caller
open_points.default_guess: Use a server-minted room_id and required display name.

open_points.subject: room-list order
open_points.text: “the project's rooms in a declared order”
open_points.question: What exact room ordering and tie-breaker are declared?
options: Creation order then room_id
Display name then room_id
Caller-managed ordinal then room_id
open_points.default_guess: Order by creation time then room_id.

open_points.subject: artifact pointer model
open_points.text: “catalogue metadata and a service-owned reference (uri, payload_ref)”
open_points.question: What complete fields identify an artifact pointer, and are uri and payload_ref both required, optional, or alternatives?
options: Both uri and payload_ref are required
Exactly one of uri or payload_ref is required
Both are optional opaque reference fields
open_points.default_guess: Require owner service, type and payload_ref; make uri optional.

open_points.subject: artifact identity and version
open_points.text: “the new version” and “unknown pointer refused”
open_points.question: What is the pointer identifier used by withdrawal, and who allocates the pointer id and version value?
options: Registry mints pointer_id and monotonically increasing version
Producer supplies pointer_id and version
The tuple project_id, type and version is the identity
open_points.default_guess: Have Registry mint pointer_id and increment an integer version per project and type.

open_points.subject: staff artifact publishing
open_points.text: “publish an artifact pointer | producer service” versus “staff ... publish for any owner service”
open_points.question: Is staff publishing part of the publish action, and how does staff select the owner service whose type rules apply?
options: Staff may publish and must name an owner service
Only producer services may publish
Staff uses a separate administrative action
open_points.default_guess: Allow staff to publish while requiring an explicit configured owner service.

open_points.subject: artifact publication transaction
open_points.text: “the previous published version of that type becomes superseded”
open_points.question: Must creation and supersession be atomic, and what happens if concurrent publishes target the same project and type?
options: Serialize atomically and assign successive versions
Reject one concurrent publication as a conflict
Permit multiple published versions temporarily
open_points.default_guess: Atomically serialize publications and preserve exactly one published version.

open_points.subject: artifact withdrawal target and archive behavior
open_points.text: “unknown pointer refused” and no archived-project case is stated
open_points.question: How is the pointer selected for withdrawal, and may its owner or staff withdraw a currently published pointer after the project is archived?
options: Select by pointer_id and allow withdrawal after archival
Select by project, type and version and refuse archived projects
Select the current project/type pointer and allow withdrawal
open_points.default_guess: Select by pointer_id and allow withdrawal after archival because it does not modify project identity.

open_points.subject: artifact history output
open_points.text: “every pointer ... each with its type, version and status”
open_points.question: What other pointer fields are returned, what named field wraps the list, and what deterministic history order applies?
options: Return complete pointer metadata under artifacts, newest version first
Return only type, version and status under items
Group pointers by type and order versions ascending
open_points.default_guess: Return complete pointer metadata under artifacts, ordered by publication time descending then pointer_id.

open_points.subject: latest-artifact failure
open_points.text: “unknown project; no published pointer of that type”
open_points.question: How can callers distinguish an unknown project, an unknown artifact type and a known type with no published pointer?
options: Distinct structured error codes
The same not-found response for all cases
Unknown type is validation failure; the other two are distinct not-found reasons
open_points.default_guess: Use distinct codes for project_not_found, artifact_type_not_configured and artifact_not_published.

open_points.subject: protected-action failures
open_points.text: “Every write needs one of them; recording, correcting, reading or erasing a customer needs the staff credential” while the action table states no missing, invalid or wrong-service credential failures
open_points.question: What observable failures result from a missing credential, an invalid credential and a valid credential lacking authority for the requested action?
options: Separate unauthenticated and forbidden failures
One generic authorization failure
Conceal protected resources as not found
open_points.default_guess: Distinguish unauthenticated from forbidden without revealing credential details.

open_points.subject: project timestamps
open_points.text: “created and updated times” and “Archiving it again ... its updated time does not move”
open_points.question: Which successful mutations move updated time, what clock and precision are used, and do idempotent create replays or no-op corrections leave it unchanged?
options: UTC server time; only actual state changes update it
UTC server time; every successful request updates it
Caller-supplied timestamps
open_points.default_guess: Use server UTC time and update it only when persisted project state changes.

open_points.subject: artifact configuration identity
open_points.text: “a list in the instance's configuration” and “one owner service of each”
open_points.question: What identifies an owner service, how does it map to the service identity named by a token, and is configuration read only at startup or allowed to change while data already exists?
options: Stable service-name strings loaded at startup
Stable service ids with live reload
Token-specific owner mappings
open_points.default_guess: Use stable service-name strings and load the mapping at startup.

open_points.subject: list envelope names
open_points.text: “items are in a named field”
open_points.question: What is the exact named field for each project, customer, room and artifact list response?
options: Resource-specific fields such as projects, customers, rooms and artifacts
A common items field
A common data field
open_points.default_guess: Use resource-specific plural field names.

open_points.subject: launch context
open_points.text: “Registry gives the launch context (project_id, optional room_id)”
open_points.question: Which Registry action returns or validates this launch context, to whom, and what failure occurs for an unknown room, a room in another project or an archived project?
options: A dedicated launch-context action
Include room_id handling in read project context
Registry merely documents values assembled by another client
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as client-assembled data validated through project context and room listing, not as a separate Registry output.

open_points.subject: remaining owner decisions
open_points.text: “None open” versus “not accepted by the owner as a whole”
open_points.question: What decision or acceptance remains before the whole State 0 can be treated as closed?
options: Owner acceptance of R0-01 through R0-05 and the boundary text
No decision remains; the status line is stale
Specific unresolved questions must be enumerated here
open_points.default_guess: Record owner acceptance of the whole document as still open.
